title: Define organism-level benchmark and LLM-organ interface
description: Replace BPC-centric model selection with a preregistered organism-level evaluation suite. acceptance_criteria: Protocol defines tasks that cannot be solved solely by a fixed language shortcut; reports language capability separately from adaptation speed, retention, transfer, causal substrate use, structural differentiation, recovery, and compute/memory cost; includes sensor/effector remapping, new-organ attachment, and lesion/recovery tests; specifies the LLM-organ state/action interface and credit boundary; GRU/transformer controls are descriptive and scoped to what they actually test; decision rules are fixed before GPU results.
notes: S1-P seed7 completed on commit4971cf7 in48m54s, all branches zero rejects. CUDA ordinal naming was reversed: creature actually ran on physical RTX2070S; no scientific effect, use GPU UUIDs henceforth. Strict result: acquisition snapshot length accuracies 99.9/96.6/64.8/31.9%, so prereg fixed-length4 acquisition gate failed. After 2k A continuation length4 reached60.4%; full B reached54.4%, full B early advantage over identical scratch+12.08pp (passes strong-transfer threshold), scratch stayed11.2% fixed4. A-control lesions: freeze internal -48.8pp, compute -48.3pp, relay -46.8pp, topology rewire -46.7pp, identity shuffle -7.3pp; state shuffle -0.7pp, memory zero -0.3pp. Thus both compute/relay tissues and learned topology are causally essential. Full C fixed4 21.0%, organ-only18.6%; changed procedure not mastered. Length8 near chance. Return-A11.98% is confounded/unidentifiable because A/B permute the same token IDs with contradictory meanings and no organ/mode cue; current B overwrites one interface rather than attaching a distinct organ. Verdict: qualified partial success—causal integrated substrate, useful whole-organism adaptation and acquisition-dependent bootstrap, but long-depth acquisition/modular reuse not yet proven. Next amend benchmark to train A to fixed4 mastery and attach distinct A/B sensor-output organs so retention and organ addition are meaningful.

title: Mixed tissue: hand-placed relay (white matter) vs all-grey at matched budget
description: Before any cell-type spawning mechanism, test whether mixed tissue helps AT ALL with hand-placed layout. Arms (3 seeds, matched params): all-grey (F0 config) vs grey+relay population wired between port regions. Relay cell = cheap near-identity transport with learned gain + time constant, no HxH rule application (~H times cheaper per cell than grey, directly relaxing the cells x steps x params constraint). Rationale: dmon/stream died of a transport deficiency (6x micro-steps moved the effective radius zero); sol S11 (maintenance floor on activity-measured flow) was the one physiology mechanism to win its full-scale gate; F0 s7 shuffle-internal +0.066 shows current homogeneous tissue is near-inert. Honest limit: composed relays are linear, so white matter buys geometry and DELAY, not expressivity -- the delay story (relay chain = learned-length delay line) is the real payoff and should replace the fixed mirror ring, which measured only +0.17. If hand-placed mixed tissue does not win, no spawning mechanism will rescue it (cheap check before expensive search).
close_reason: Superseded by F5 (DMON-1 informed growth): the hand-placed/random-placement plan rested on an incoherent premise. White matter is definitionally positional -- a relay at a random position is noise, not a weak relay -- so type and placement are not separable for this cell type. Also, fable's connectome is ALREADY randomly wired and F0 measured that tissue as near-inert (shuffle delta 0.045-0.066), so a random-placement arm would have reproduced the known failure regime and returned a false negative. Random survives as the proposal-informativeness control inside F5.
